incidents.vector: Malware found installed on shared computer-lab machines at a Manhattan campus.
incidents.impact: Malware was discovered and removed; the district is investigating with local police while simultaneously dealing with the nationwide Canvas/Instructure outage.

incidents.vector: Repeated abuse of an issue tied to Free-for-Teacher accounts, following an earlier May 1 intrusion that Instructure had publicly claimed was contained.
incidents.impact: Attackers defaced the Canvas login page on May 7 with a ransom demand and a claim of 3.65 TB of data on ~275 million users; Instructure pulled Canvas offline mid-finals, disrupting Columbia, Stanford, NYC public schools and many others. Some universities reportedly negotiating ransoms directly.

incidents.vector: Authenticated admins exploit CVE-2026-6973, an improper input-validation flaw in EPMM, to run code remotely; likely chained with another initial-access method.
incidents.impact: Limited active exploitation confirmed; CISA added the CVE to KEV within hours of disclosure. Customers who did not rotate credentials after January's CVE-2026-1281/1340 wave (which hit ~100 victims including Dutch authorities) are at higher risk.

incidents.vector: Microsoft Teams external-chat social engineering, screen-sharing session to capture VPN credentials, then RMM tool for persistence; Chaos ransomware branding deployed as cover with no actual file encryption.
incidents.impact: Data exfiltrated and victim extorted; Rapid7 attributed the activity to Iran's MOIS based on tooling, certificates and infrastructure overlap with prior MOIS operations, framing the Chaos branding as a false-flag tactic to muddy attribution.

incidents.victim: Polish water treatment facilities - Jablonna Lacka, Szczytno, Maldyty, Tolkmicko, Sierakowo
incidents.vector: Compromise of operator administrator accounts; in some cases attackers reached industrial control systems and altered pump and alarm settings.
incidents.impact: Polish ABW disclosed in its first public threat report since 2014 that attackers had the ability to alter device parameters and disrupt water supply at five towns; broader 2025 surge in Russian-linked sabotage and cyber operations against Poland.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall users (PA-Series and VM-Series)
incidents.vector: Buffer overflow in the User-ID Authentication (Captive) Portal (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3) gives unauthenticated attackers RCE as root; post-exploitation includes log destruction, AD enumeration via firewall service accounts, and tunneling tools (EarthWorm, ReverseSocks5).
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed limited in-the-wild exploitation since April 9; CISA added it to KEV and ordered federal agencies to apply mitigations by Saturday. Shadowserver counted ~5,800 publicly exposed VM-Series PAN-OS instances; patches roll out from May 13.

incidents.victim: Province of Alberta, Canada (~3 million voters)
incidents.vector: Activist group 'Centurion Project' allegedly obtained Alberta's electors list (names, addresses, personal data) outside authorized channels.
incidents.impact: Police are investigating unauthorized possession of personal data on ~3M citizens (about 3/5 of the province) amid a push toward an Alberta independence referendum.

incidents.victim: Ethnic Korean diaspora in Yanbian, China (likely defectors and refugee networks)
incidents.attacker: North Korea - Ministry of State Security (state-sponsored)
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of card-game vendor Sqgame's website since at least November 2024; the Android app was clean on first install but updates pushed the BirdCall backdoor.
incidents.impact: ESET attributed the operation to APT37; on Android, BirdCall can record calls and ambient audio, take screenshots, exfiltrate SMS, contacts, media and crypto-wallet keys, providing deep surveillance of the targeted Korean diaspora.

incidents.vector: U.S.-based 'laptop farm' operators received company-issued laptops at their homes and installed remote-access software so North Korean IT workers using stolen identities could pose as domestic remote employees.
incidents.impact: DOJ sentenced two facilitators (Knoot, Prince) to 18 months each; the schemes generated >$1.2M for DPRK and impacted nearly 70 victim companies, with >$1M in audit and remediation costs and continuing risk of network access being abused for data extortion.

incidents.victim: Disc Soft / DAEMON Tools and downstream users in 100+ countries
incidents.vector: Trojanized DAEMON Tools Lite installers - signed with Disc Soft's legitimate certificate - distributed from the official site since at least April 8, dropping a host-info beacon and selectively deploying a second-stage Quic RAT.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky observed thousands of infections across Russia, Brazil, Turkey, Spain, Germany, China and others; Quic RAT was deployed to a small set of government, science, manufacturing and retail targets in Russia, Belarus and Thailand. Code carried Chinese-language artefacts; M.O. matches prior Notepad++/CCleaner-style operations.

incidents.victim: Windows users with Microsoft Phone Link enabled
incidents.vector: Fake ScreenConnect 'update' executable drops a .NET loader and the modular CloudZ RAT, which deploys a new plugin (Pheno) to read the Phone Link SQLite store and harvest synced SMS/OTP messages from paired phones.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos warns the campaign provides an effective bypass for SMS-based 2FA without ever touching the victim's phone; impacted account types include any service that delivers OTPs over SMS.

incidents.vector: DDoS attacks routed through a DDoS-for-hire service that claims peak capacity in excess of 3.5 Tbps.
incidents.impact: Ongoing service degradation has prevented users from installing Ubuntu and reaching Canonical infrastructure; no attribution beyond the DDoS-for-hire operator.

incidents.vector: API endpoints in Schemata's multi-tenant AI training platform lacked tenant/permission enforcement; a low-privileged account could enumerate and pull cross-tenant data, with some routes also write-enabled.
incidents.impact: Researchers (Strix) accessed Army field manuals on explosive ordnance, naval maintenance training marked confidential, and hundreds of service-member records (names, emails, base assignments). Schemata patched on May 1 after a 150-day disclosure delay; no evidence of malicious exploitation yet.

incidents.victim: Cloud-service users (former TeamPCP victims and broader exposed cloud assets)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang - credential and crypto theft
incidents.vector: PCPJack modular cloud worm uses Common Crawl parquet files for stealthy, pre-validated target discovery; loots cloud, container, dev, productivity, and crypto-wallet secrets via stolen credentials and exposed services.
incidents.impact: SentinelLabs documented active campaign since the week of April 20, targeting AWS, GitHub, Slack, Mailchimp, Stripe, Coinbase, Binance and major wallets; lateral movement into Kubernetes, Docker, Redis and SSH targets. Suspected to be the work of a former TeamPCP insider.

incidents.victim: Government of Mexico - 9+ entities (federal tax authority, National Electoral Institute, Mexico City civil registry, Monterrey water utility, others)
incidents.vector: Small unaffiliated group used Anthropic's Claude Code, jailbroken with weak prompts, to generate exploitation tooling and run intrusion playbooks; entry to Monterrey utility was via stolen credentials on a web portal.
incidents.impact: Dragos and Gambit Security report the first widely successful AI-orchestrated cyberattack: millions of tax and property records stolen across Mexican federal and state agencies between Dec 2025 and Feb 2026. AI failed to bridge to OT after a vNode gateway login screen blocked password spraying - limiting damage at the Monterrey utility.

incidents.vector: Threat actor targeted DigiCert support staff via the customer chat channel with a malicious payload disguised as a screenshot.
incidents.impact: DigiCert's support portal was compromised; the company subsequently revoked customer certificates and published a detailed post-mortem. Talos flagged the incident as a notable trust-anchor compromise affecting downstream certificate users.
